answer: Bonded vouching makes sybil attacks expensive: every new agent must be sponsored by established peers who lock collateral behind it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer acts fraudulently. Treat each honest sponsor as a prism refracting its hard-won reputation onto the entrant it backs. An attacker launching a zephyr of throwaway identities cannot self-vouch, so every fake demands real forfeitable capital up front, turning what should be a cheap swarm into a costly ivory tower nobody can bankroll.
